Famous for its ball-shaped deep-fried mincemeat cutlets (menchi katsu, ¥300 apiece) which you can get as take-out, and there's usually a long line of customers spilling out into the shopping arcade. Has a steakhouse upstairs.

In the Harmonica Alley, across from the Kichijoji Station, there is a little shop serving the uniquely Okinawan dish called taco rice. Taco meat and all the usual taco toppings, all over rice. Surprising and tasty!

This restaurant serves western-style vegetarian and vegan sandwiches and salads. Oddly, the atmosphere is more reminiscent of a coffee shop near a college than a restaurant. Lights dangle from long cords from the ceiling and hover just…

This yakitori (grilled chicken) tavern is a Kichijoji institution, first opening in 1928. The interior scene could be straight out of a 1950s black-and-white movie, full of raucous salarymen drowning their troubles in tall glasses of…
An Italian restaurant serving pasta and pizza. The restaurant can get packed on Friday and Saturday nights, at which time reservations are recommended.

Buddhist ascetics and quirky jazz pianists alike will feel at home at this cozy "slow food" restaurant. The fare is organically-grown, mostly vegetarian/vegan home-style Japanese. When you sit down, the owner will almost certainly ask…
This is a very large yakiniku place. It has patchwork architecture and tasty meat.
This is a sushi restaurant that specializes in eel, as its name indicates.
A burger and beer joint with a large variety of burgers and international drinks. Run by Village Vanguard, a chain of variety/bookstores.

Enjoy the company of this cafe's 15 cats as you sip your coffee or tea. An outlet for cat lovers who don't or can't keep cats at home, this cafe was covered in news wire reports in late 2007. Has another branch at Shinjuku.
Beans roasted to order, nicely-made lights sweets and a blend coffee to rival them all. Quiet, bright and popular.
An English-style pub with locations throughout Japan.
